caveat: the k>=3 repeat traces read all-zero rather than all-one because pin control was still armed, so the iio_attr re-arm of RX1 to 52 dB before each repeat was silently ignored (see armed_write_ab.json) and the index walked down 2 per repeat until it fell below the overload point. Only the first two repeats test what was intended.
method: drive CH1 into large-ADC overload, step the gain down with a CTRL_IN pin edge (a shell-builtin GPIO write, ~100s of us, versus 67 ms for an iio_attr write), then sample CTRL_OUT5 in a tight builtin loop
next: belongs to the FPGA stage, alongside the minimum-pulse-width question
prediction: an asserted large-overload bit stays high until the gain changes, then returns low for at least the Peak Overload Wait Time

provenance.harness: TX2 -> 30 dB pad -> bare SMA tee -> RX1/RX2 (tee has ~0 dB port-to-port isolation; see docs/learnings.md harness entry)
provenance.source: own TX2 fpga_dds tone at +100 kHz, TX2 hardwaregain 0 dB (full scale)

reading: No 1->0->1 excursion was seen after the gain step at 322 us sampling granularity. That bounds any post-change blank at under 322 us but neither confirms nor refutes the latch-and-blank behaviour, so open item O-3 stays open. This is the pre-declared H4/H5 resolution limit in section 2, and it is worse than budgeted: reading a GPIO value file costs 322 us, not the 134 us measured on a plain sysfs attribute.
